backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 linearly up to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Change only the momentum value fed to the Muon optimizer each step; leave all other optimizer logic untouched.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. This saves wall-clock per step inside the fixed 300 s budget, so more optimizer steps fit. Keep the same quintic coefficients and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: For each matrix parameter updated by Muon, multiply the orthogonalized update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) before applying MATRIX_LR, so tall matrices (MLP up-projection, embedding-like shapes) receive proportionally larger steps. Keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 and all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon learning-rate scaling

backlog.spec: Raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 and keep every other hyperparameter fixed. The lm_head is the only Adam-trained output projection, so this tests whether the output layer is under-trained at the current rate.
backlog.title: Higher unembedding (lm_head) learning rate

backlog.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and set the Adam epsilon for the embedding group to 1e-10 so that sparse token rows still update meaningfully. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Lower embedding learning rate

backlog.spec: Scale WEIGHT_DECAY for the Muon matrix group by the current LR multiplier and additionally by (1 - progress), where progress is the fraction of the 300 s time budget elapsed, so decay fades to zero by the end of training. Apply it only where the cautious mask already allows updates.
backlog.title: Cautious weight decay with linear decay to zero

backlog.spec: Set weight decay to zero for embeddings, lm_head and all per-layer scalar parameters, keeping WEIGHT_DECAY=0.2 only on the Muon-trained 2D matrices. Implement by passing weight_decay=0 for the Adam groups and leaving the Muon group unchanged.
backlog.title: Weight decay restricted to matrix parameters

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the final 70% of the time budget, keeping WARMUP_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC unchanged. This tests whether a longer cooldown improves the final checkpoint.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown phase

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so that all learning rates ramp linearly from zero over the first 2% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. Keep the rest of the schedule code unchanged.
backlog.title: Short warmup before full learning rate

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown multiplier with a cosine curve: multiplier = 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * p)) where p is the fraction of the warmdown window completed, applied to all learning-rate groups. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5 and FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.0.
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped warmdown

backlog.spec: Ramp the learning rates of the Adam-trained groups (embedding, lm_head, scalars) linearly from 10% to 100% over the first 200 optimizer steps, while Muon matrix learning rate follows the normal schedule from step 0. This protects the high-LR scalar and embedding groups during early training.
backlog.title: Adam-group learning-rate warmup

backlog.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 and double it at fixed time fractions (at 25% and 50% of the budget) up to 2**19, adjusting gradient-accumulation steps accordingly. Early steps are cheaper and more numerous; the final phase uses the full batch.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp during training

backlog.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 while keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64, so each step uses half as many tokens and the 300 s budget yields roughly twice as many optimizer updates. Keep all learning rates unchanged.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch size

backlog.spec: Add global gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 on all trainable parameters after the backward pass and before the optimizer steps. This stabilizes the high learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, SCALAR_LR 0.5) in the early phase.
backlog.title: Gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss, computed over the vocabulary dimension of the lm_head outputs. This keeps logit magnitudes bounded without changing the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Output logit z-loss

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to the final logits as logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy loss in training and inside the forward pass used for evaluation. This bounds extreme predictions and often improves bits-per-byte in small models.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding matrix and scale the logits by 1/sqrt(model_dim) to compensate. Remove the separate lm_head parameter group so UNEMBEDDING_LR is no longer used, and keep EMBEDDING_LR for the shared matrix.
backlog.title: Tied input and output embeddings

backlog.spec: Store the residual stream after each of the first half of the transformer blocks and add it back, through a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0, into the matching block in the second half in reverse order. Keep the total layer count DEPTH=8 and all other modules unchanged.
backlog.title: U-Net style encoder-decoder skip connections

backlog.spec: After the query and key RMS normalization in each attention layer, multiply by a learnable per-head gain vector initialized to 1 (one per head, separate for q and k). Keep the attention scale otherwise unchanged and store the gains in the scalar parameter group.
backlog.title: QK-norm with learnable per-head gain

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU MLP whose hidden width is set to about 2/3 of 4*model_dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, so the parameter count stays close to the baseline. Keep the same residual and normalization structure.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP instead of ReLU-squared

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 52 so model_dim is about 520, rounded to 512 to keep it a multiple of HEAD_DIM=128. Keep the window pattern, learning rates and batch settings the same, so the run tests depth against width at similar compute.
backlog.title: Deeper and narrower model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so model_dim is about 510, rounded to 512 to keep it a multiple of HEAD_DIM=128. Keep all other hyperparameters unchanged. This trades layers for faster steps within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Shallower and wider model

backlog.spec: Use grouped-query attention with num_kv_heads set to 2 for the key and value projections while keeping the number of query heads unchanged. Repeat the key and value heads across query groups before attention. This reduces attention parameters and memory traffic at the same model width.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with 2 KV heads

backlog.spec: Change the rotary position embedding base from 10000 to 100000 to extend the usable positional frequency range. Keep the head dimension at HEAD_DIM=128 and leave the attention code otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Larger rotary base

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SL" so half the layers use the full context and half use the half-context sliding window. Keep the final layer forced to full context as in the existing code.
backlog.title: Alternating sliding-window pattern

backlog.spec: Scale the initialization of each block's attention output projection and MLP output projection by 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) so the residual stream variance stays bounded as depth grows. Apply only at parameter initialization, not in the forward pass.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled residual initialization

backlog.spec: Train the first 30% of the time budget with sequence length 512 and a proportionally larger number of sequences per device batch to keep tokens per step constant, then switch to the full sequence length. Keep the data loader interface unchanged and only change how the batch is reshaped.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Before the final evaluation call, copy the EMA weights into the model. Do not modify the evaluation call or the summary printing.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average for final weights

backlog.spec: Enable TF32 matmul and cuDNN TF32 flags, and set torch.compile to use the default mode with dynamic=False. Use the fused implementation for AdamW where available. These are pure speed changes that should not affect the optimization math.
backlog.title: Throughput settings for compilation and matmuls

backlog.spec: Initialize the lm_head weight to exactly zero and set the embedding init standard deviation to 1e-3 so the model starts from uniform predictions with stable gradients. Leave all block initialization unchanged.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized output head

backlog.spec: In the attention block, compute each layer's value vectors V as usual, then mix in the first layer's V: V_l = lerp(V_l, V_0, sigmoid(a_l)) where a_l is a new learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0 (so the mix starts at 0.5). Layer 0 uses its own V. Keep Q/K and the rest of the block unchanged, and add the scalars to the Adam scalar group with SCALAR_LR. This gives later layers direct access to early token features, which can help a short-budget run.
backlog.title: Value residual from first layer

backlog.spec: Add a second embedding table indexed by a hash of the previous and current token, (prev * 1000003 + cur) mod 2**16 (or a similar cheap hash), with dimension model_dim and zero-initialized weights. Add its output to the token embedding before the first block, scaled by a learnable scalar initialized to 1. Train this table with EMBEDDING_LR on Adam like the token embedding. It is a cheap way to give the model extra bigram capacity without changing depth or width.
backlog.title: Bigram hash embedding added to residual stream

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block from sequential x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x)) to parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing one pre-norm. Keep the existing per-layer residual scalars and window pattern. This removes one normalization and one serial dependency per layer, which can increase throughput within the fixed 300 s budget. Verify that the model still compiles and that the first-step loss is comparable.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP residual blocks

backlog.spec: Apply RoPE only to the first half of each head's q and k dimensions and leave the second half unrotated (position-free). Adjust the rotary cos/sin cache to size head_dim/2 so the rotation covers only that half, and concatenate the unrotated half back before attention. Keep HEAD_DIM and all other settings unchanged. This lets some channels carry content-only matching that generalizes across positions.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embeddings on half the head dimensions

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon matrix learning rate per layer by a depth factor: lr_l = MATRIX_LR * (0.85 ** (layer_index)) for block parameters, with the lm_head and embeddings unchanged. Implement it by giving each Muon parameter group its own lr at construction, and keep the existing warmdown schedule multiplying all groups. Deeper layers then take smaller steps, which can stabilize the residual stream when the learning rate is high.
backlog.title: Depth-decayed Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Keep 5 Newton-Schulz iterations (reducing the count was clearly harmful), but replace the polynomial coefficients used in the Muon orthogonalization with the more aggressive set (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) that pushes singular values toward 1 faster. Keep the normalization step and the rest of the Muon update unchanged. Only the coefficient tuple changes, so the diff is a one-line edit and the effect is isolated to how orthogonalized updates are shaped.
backlog.title: Alternative Newton-Schulz polynomial coefficients

backlog.spec: Add one extra lightweight prediction head that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden state, using a separate linear layer initialized to zero. Add its cross-entropy loss to the main loss with weight 0.2 during training only. Do not change the evaluation path or the main lm_head. The auxiliary loss gives the trunk a denser training signal per step, and the extra head is only used during training, so inference cost is unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head

backlog.spec: Multiply the per-token cross-entropy by a weight w(t) that ramps linearly from 0.5 at the first position of each sequence to 1.0 at the last position, then renormalize so the mean weight over the sequence is 1. Compute the weighted mean over tokens in the batch. Keep the optimizer, schedule, and evaluation unchanged. This shifts gradient emphasis toward later positions, where the model has more context and the bits-per-byte metric benefits most.
backlog.title: Position-dependent loss weighting

backlog.spec: Apply dropout with rate 0.05 to the token embedding output during training only, using the standard inverted-dropout scaling, and disable it under model.eval(). Do not apply dropout inside the attention or MLP blocks. Because the run is short (about one pass over the data at most), mild input-side regularization may help generalization to the validation set. Keep the random seed lines untouched.
backlog.title: Token embedding dropout

backlog.spec: Use label smoothing with epsilon 0.02 in the training cross-entropy only, by passing label_smoothing=0.02 to the loss call when model.training is true. Keep the evaluation loss exactly as it is, unsmoothed. This softens overconfident predictions on the 8192-way output distribution and can reduce overfitting to frequent tokens, while leaving the metric computation untouched.
backlog.title: Label smoothing on the training loss

backlog.spec: The metric is bits per byte, but training averages cross-entropy per token, so tokens that span more UTF-8 bytes are underweighted. Precompute, once at startup, the UTF-8 byte length of each vocabulary entry by decoding it with the tokenizer already used in train.py. In the training loss, multiply each target token's cross-entropy by its byte length, then divide by the sum of byte lengths in the batch instead of the token count. Leave the evaluation path and the final summary printing untouched. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy

backlog.spec: Keep a copy x0 of the normalized token embedding taken before the first block. Before each transformer block, replace the residual stream with x = a_l * x + b_l * x0, where a_l and b_l are learnable per-layer scalars. Initialize a_l to 1 and b_l to 0, and put them in the existing scalar-parameter Adam group. This gives every layer a direct path to the input embedding, a bolder variant of plain residual connections.
backlog.title: Per-layer mixing with the initial embedding

backlog.spec: Add a second embedding table with the vocabulary size and the attention model dimension, used only for values. In every other layer, including the last one, add a learned gate times the lookup of the current input token's value embedding to the attention value vectors before the attention computation. Initialize the table to zero and the gate to a small constant, and train both with the Adam group that handles embeddings. Costs one extra table of parameters and no extra sequence-length compute.
backlog.title: Token-indexed value embeddings

backlog.spec: Keep rotary position embeddings in most layers, but in every fourth block (layers 4, 8, and so on, counting from 1) skip the rotary rotation on queries and keys so that attention is position-agnostic in those layers. The sliding-window pattern stays as it is. Make the choice a single constant list so it can be changed without touching the attention code. This tests whether a few content-only heads help a short-context model.
backlog.title: No-position-embedding layers every fourth block

backlog.spec: Training sequences are packed, so attention can cross document boundaries. Identify the document separator token by the BOS id already available in train.py. For each position, build a mask that blocks attention to earlier tokens that lie before the most recent separator in the same row. Combine this mask with the existing causal and sliding-window masks. Use the same mask in the training forward pass only. Keep the evaluation path unchanged.
backlog.title: Document-boundary attention masking

backlog.spec: During training only, for each forward pass and each block except the first and last, sample a Bernoulli keep decision with probability 0.9 for each example in the batch. If a block is dropped, pass the residual stream through unchanged for that block. Scale the block's residual update by 1/0.9 when it is kept so the expected activation stays the same. Disable dropping in evaluation and in the final summary. This is a regularizer on depth that is cheap in code.
backlog.title: Stochastic layer dropping

backlog.spec: Change FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1, so the learning rate decays to 10 percent of its initial value by the end of the 300-second budget instead of to zero. Keep the warmdown start and the linear shape as they are. Apply the floor to every parameter group, including Muon, Adam, and the scalar groups. Change nothing else. This tests whether a non-zero end learning rate helps a short run that stops before convergence.
backlog.title: Final LR floor instead of zero

backlog.spec: Starting at 70 percent of the time budget, after each optimizer step, add the current parameters into a running sum held in float32 on the GPU and count the number of additions. At the end of training, replace the model weights with the average of the saved snapshots before the harness evaluation runs. Do not modify the evaluation call itself. This replaces the EMA attempt, which was likely broken, with a simple uniform average over the warmdown phase, which is a different and safer weight-averaging scheme.
backlog.title: Uniform averaging of late checkpoints

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam update for the token embedding and the lm_head weight with a Lion-style update. Keep a momentum buffer with beta1 = 0.9, and at each step update the weight by lr times the sign of the interpolation between the momentum and the current gradient, with decoupled weight decay of 0.1 times lr. Keep the existing EMBEDDING_LR and UNEMBEDDING_LR values, but scale them by 0.3 because sign updates have unit magnitude per coordinate. Matrix parameters stay on Muon and the scalars stay on Adam.
backlog.title: Sign-momentum update for embedding and lm_head

backlog.spec: Move the lm_head weight, which has shape vocabulary by model dimension, from the Adam group into the Muon group, so its gradient update is orthogonalized with the same Newton-Schulz routine that Muon uses for hidden matrices. Use a learning rate of 0.02 for this matrix, and scale the Newton-Schulz output by the square root of max(1, rows divided by columns) so the update magnitude matches the hidden matrices. Keep the embedding table on Adam. This is a single change to parameter grouping and one learning rate.
backlog.title: Orthogonalized updates for lm_head

backlog.spec: Keep the 6 transformer blocks but run the whole stack twice per forward pass (12 effective layers, 6 unique sets of weights). Add a learned per-pass scalar (initialized to 1 for pass 1 and 0.5 for pass 2) that multiplies each block's residual update so the two passes can differ. Use the same rotary positions and attention windows on both passes. Leave the optimizer grouping unchanged, with shared parameters placed in the same Muon and Adam groups as before. Expect fewer steps per 300 s, so keep DEPTH and ASPECT_RATIO fixed and let the step count fall naturally.
backlog.title: Shared-weight looped block stack

backlog.spec: Replace each block's ReLU-squared MLP with a small mixture of 4 experts and top-1 routing. Each expert is a narrower MLP with hidden width equal to the original width divided by 4, so active FLOPs per token stay about the same. The router is a linear layer on the normalized input, trained with Adam at the scalar LR. Add a load-balancing auxiliary loss with coefficient 0.01 that penalizes the mean router probability times the fraction of tokens routed to each expert. Route with a plain argmax over the router logits and scale the expert output by its softmax probability.
backlog.title: Top-1 mixture-of-experts MLP

backlog.spec: After the scaled-dot-product attention and before the output projection, multiply each head's output elementwise by a sigmoid gate computed from the normalized block input through a small linear layer (n_embd to n_head, one gate value per head per token). Initialize the gate weights to zero and the gate bias to +2 so the gate starts near 0.88 and the model begins close to the baseline. Train the gate weights with the same group as the attention projections. This adds one small matmul per block and no other change to the training loop.
backlog.title: Gated attention output

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam-group schedule for embeddings, lm_head and scalars with a schedule-free update: keep a fast iterate z updated by Adam and a running average x of the iterates, and evaluate with x. Use beta1 = 0.9 for the interpolation, keep the existing learning rates for those groups, and drop the time-based LR warmdown for these groups only. Muon groups keep the current warmdown schedule. At the end of training, switch the model parameters to x before the evaluation call without changing the evaluation code itself.
backlog.title: Schedule-free AdamW for non-Muon groups

backlog.spec: Set the Muon momentum to a constant 0.90 for the entire run instead of the current value, keeping Nesterov enabled and all other Muon settings unchanged. The aim is to test whether the default high momentum over-smooths updates in a short 300 s run where fast early progress matters more than noise averaging. Also report the value of the effective update norm at step 100 in the log so the change can be checked. Do not add any warmup for momentum, since that is a separate idea.
backlog.title: Constant Muon momentum sweep

backlog.spec: Replace the single linear warmdown with a two-cycle schedule over the time budget. The first cycle runs at full LR from 0 to 55% of the budget and then decays with a cosine to 0.3x the peak. At 55% of the budget the LR jumps back to 1.0x peak and decays with a cosine to 0 at the end. All learning rates (Muon and Adam groups) follow the same multiplier. Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0 and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0. The purpose is to test whether a mid-run restart helps the model escape a sharp basin before the final anneal.
backlog.title: Single warm restart in the LR schedule

backlog.spec: Add one learned scalar parameter log_temp, initialized to 0, and divide the final logits by exp(log_temp) before the cross-entropy loss. Train log_temp with the scalar Adam group at SCALAR_LR, with no weight decay. This lets the model adjust the sharpness of its output distribution during training, which can matter when the LR is high early in the run. Do not change the loss normalization or the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Learned output logit temperature

backlog.spec: Apply dropout with p = 0.1 to the hidden activations of each MLP, after the ReLU-squared nonlinearity and before the down projection. Enable dropout only in training mode, so the evaluation path is unchanged. Keep all other settings the same. Expect a small regularization effect; the test is whether the model is limited by overfitting in the 300 s budget, which is unlikely at this size, so measure the train and validation loss gap in the log.
backlog.title: MLP activation dropout

backlog.spec: Double the training sequence length (for example from 1024 to 2048 tokens) and halve DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE so the number of tokens per micro-batch stays constant and memory does not change. The total batch size of 2**19 tokens per optimizer step is unchanged, so the number of optimizer steps is unchanged. Keep the sliding-window pattern but scale the short-window size with the new sequence length so that the S layers still see half of the context. Make sure the data loading uses the new sequence length, and keep the harness import line and evaluation call unchanged.
backlog.title: Longer sequences at constant tokens per micro-step

backlog.spec: Change the standard deviation used to initialize the token embedding matrix from its current value to 1.0 times the standard deviation of the default PyTorch normal initialization (about 1.0) and keep the lm_head initialization as it is. Because the embedding LR is high (0.6 under Adam), a much larger initial scale may change early learning dynamics. Make this change as a single init constant so it is easy to revert. Do not change the EMBEDDING_LR value in this experiment.
backlog.title: Embedding initialization scale sweep

memo: Incumbent is slot 5 (DEPTH 6, ASPECT_RATIO 85): 1.1021, delta -0.0124, from a single run, so replicate it first. The shallow-wide model helped because it fits more steps into 300 s. Other changes were neutral or worse: SwiGLU +0.0017, parallel blocks +0.0128, GQA +0.0011, q/k gain +0.0003, warmdown 0.7 +0.0015, Newton-Schulz 3 iterations +0.0457, tied embeddings +0.0105, LR warmup +0.0106, position-weighted loss +0.0036, parameter averaging +0.0044. EMA scored 2.2624 and was likely broken. Slots 10 and 11 failed to patch, so those ideas are untested. Two small gains were rejected as marginal: UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.008 (1.1009, -0.0012) and gradient clipping (-0.0035, measured against the old incumbent). Next: replicate slot 5, then stack UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.008 and clipping on it. Try DEPTH 4 or 5, other ASPECT_RATIO values, and batch size. Skip further architecture tweaks. Rewrite the failed patches carefully.
